paras: Emoia campbelli, also known commonly as Campbell's skink, the montane emo skink, and the Vitilevu mountain treeskink, is a species of lizard in the family Scincidae. The species is endemic to the island of Viti Levu in Fiji.
The specific name, campbelli, is in honor of geologist John Campbell who collected the holotype.
The preferred natural habitat of E. campbelli is forest, at altitudes of 700–1,000 m (2,300–3,300 ft).
E. campbelli is arboreal, living in the forest canopy, and sheltering in epiphytic myrmecophytes (ant plants).
E. campbelli is oviparous. Clutch size is two eggs, which are laid in the chambers of ant plants.
